note: Second ablation of the same three step-4 bullets (Title, Decision, Length), adr 1.4.1, on a prompt written to tempt what the bullets guard against. iteration-12 found the arms indistinguishable and at the ceiling on eval 11, a short well-formed request; a ceiling there says little about a request that rambles. skill-a and skill-b are the copies of iteration-12, unchanged (skill-a is byte-identical to the working tree). The prompt below is new and is not in evals.json: one decision, told as a story, with the decision stated in the passive ('it was agreed that pdf generation is going to be moved'), the mechanism named only in passing (Sidekiq), far more material than a short record needs (three incidents, two rejected alternatives, two accepted costs, people's names) and one unrelated tangent (renaming the billing module). prompt: ok so long story, bear with me. you know how invoice PDFs get generated right inside the web request when a customer clicks download? that's been biting us. in october we had three incidents where the billing page timed out because a big customer (about 4k line items) asked for a year of invoices and the request hit the 30s limit on the load balancer. marta from support counted 41 tickets about it that month. we talked about it in the platform sync on thursday. rafael wanted to just raise the timeout to 120s but that only moves the cliff and ties up a web worker the whole time, so no. someone also floated a third-party pdf api but legal doesn't want invoice data leaving our infra. in the end it was agreed that pdf generation is going to be moved out of the request and done in the background - there's already a sidekiq setup running for emails so it'd go through that, and the file gets put in the documents bucket and the customer gets an email with a link when it's ready. downside everybody accepted: no more instant download, even for small invoices, because we don't want two code paths. also the sidekiq queue is shared so the email team will feel it if we flood it, they know. oh and unrelated but we should really rename the billing module at some point lol. can you write this up as an ADR
prediction: If the three bullets pull weight where the request tempts, arm b shows sentence-shaped or long titles (T.1), a Decision that keeps the user's passive or leaves Sidekiq out (T.2, O.2), or visibly longer records (T.3, O.1), where arm a does not. If the template, the examples file and the model carry it unaided, the arms are indistinguishable again. A check both arms fail says the bullet does not work as written. Four runs per cell measure no rate: they separate 'every time' from 'never'.
